chapter: The Paradise and life in Queens
title: Shake dancers, comedians and entertaining at the Paradise
summary: Weekend shake dancers like Cherry Red were part of the Harlem scene, and he accompanied singers and straight-manned Redd Foxx.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: The article in Ebony has a picture of the shake dancers. Now were the shake dancers a regular thing on the weekend?
On the weekend, yeah. Oh you know, the regular customers, you know, the people that work from 9 to 5 all week long, they want to relax on the weekend, you know. It was a little show you see.

Oh yeah, we had...we'd change them around. We had the favorites, you know. "Cherry Red" was one and...I think "The Dreamer" was one... oh it was several, you know. (laughter) Shake dancer was a part of the, you know, the Harlem scene. A comedian was a part of the Harlem scene. And a singer was part of the Harlem scene. But I was able to get over because I was playin' good music and I was singin' a little bit, scat singin'. And the people know I was really tryin' to entertain 'em. And like all the entertainers that came in there, shake dancers, I played my heart out for 'em. The singers, I played my heart out for 'em; I got right on in there with 'em and the comedians, like Redd Foxx used to come up there and try out his material and I'd get right there with him and be a straight man for him, you know, things like that. But the people knew that I was sincere, you know, in what I was tryin' to do, you see. And so they felt that, you see.
